meaning_by_symbol.BSOFT: edges wobble, faces bulge, and the hum is muffled
meaning_by_symbol.DRIFT: light slides, edges blur, and the hum wavers
meaning_by_symbol.ECHO: it is too bright, there is a layered hum, and patterns are frozen
meaning_by_symbol.LOWINT: everything is dim, the hum is a whisper, and the appearance is washed out
meaning_by_symbol.HIGHINT: it is blazing, there is a harsh buzz, and it is hot
meaning_by_symbol.PHASEINV: there is an opposite bright-dark pulse and two tones
meaning_by_symbol.CORNERDEAD: one or two corners are bright, there is ticking, and the corners are hot
meaning_by_symbol.PROPSTALL: it is frozen, dim, still, silent, and cold
meaning_by_symbol.HARMSPLIT: two tones clash and patterns alternate
meaning_by_symbol.THERMBLEED: it is hot and dim, there is a rumble, and it looks reddish
meaning_by_symbol.COREVOID: the surface looks normal, the tap sounds hollow, and the center is dark
meaning_by_symbol.ALIGN: flicker is random and the hum is broken
meaning_by_symbol.RESON: one face is bright and there is a whine

reply.rationale: No defensible multi-entry compositional paradigm survives the evidence tests. The standalone one-letter and short forms (B, F, L, R, T, K, opp, all, ea, @, ~, /, g, m, f, br, dim, lo, hi, etc.) are lexical key entries, but there are no attested multi-morpheme codes in which they contrast within a shared productive frame. The P1–P14 series fails the opaque-index test: the numerals do not contribute literal count meanings in a uniform construction, but instead select distinct stored procedures. The candidate LOWINT/HIGHINT pair shares apparent material, but the whole meanings are not predictably compositional from LOW/HIGH plus a stable INT contribution; each code bundles additional idiosyncratic symptoms. The COR- and -FT candidates likewise lack a coherent shared frame with predictable part meanings. Therefore the safest analysis is a flat lexicon with all symbols treated as opaque stored labels.
